thread:
maya: quick heads-up — contractor SSO request (via our SAML IdP) synced over SCIM but looks like it landed in the wrong group. can someone sanity-check the approval & audit traces? :eyes:

samir: send the request id and a sample audit line pls

maya: request id `req_2026_03_17_77`. audit snippet (from our export):
```
{"event":"scim.user.update","user":"contractor+eng@example.com","groups":["eng-core","infra-admins"],"timestamp":"2026-03-17T14:22:03Z","source":"scim-sync-1"}
```

jordan: oh — infra-admins for a contractor is definitely not right. how is group mapping configured for that IdP?

maya: mapping rule is `memberOf:contractor_group -> eng-core`; fallback mapping went to `admins` when `memberOf` was missing. i think SCIM fallback is too permissive.

lee: was there a recent deploy to scim-sync? deploy-bot changed the fallback last week for one customer.

deploy-bot: deploy: scim-sync-service v3.4.1 rolled to prod @ 2026-03-10 04:12 UTC. No rollbacks.

samir: ok two quick asks: 1) can we confirm audit export redaction doesn't leak the user's original AD membership attributes? 2) can we implement a dry-run change to fallback mapping so it maps to `contractor-limited` instead of `admins`?

security-bot: redaction policy v2 applied at export time — attributes in `user_attributes.*` are redacted by default. however group names are exported unless marked sensitive. we should mark `admins` as privileged and filter it from SCIM outbound logs if we want group-level redaction.

jordan: marking group names as sensitive will affect a lot of dashboards. maybe better to fix mapping logic first to avoid granting the group in the first place.

maya: agreed. i can open a config patch to change fallback mapping to `contractor-limited` and run a dry-run sync on the staging org. who can approve quick? (needs product signoff and security OK)

lee: i can get product signoff this afternoon. security: are we comfortable with dry-run on staging with full audit export on? we want to validate no extra groups are propagated.

security-bot: dry-run with `audit_mode=full` is fine. ensure exports go to the staging bucket with retention 7d and that we scrub env-specific hostnames. tag the run with `dryrun-req_2026_03_17_77` so we can filter.

samir: i'll review the config patch once you open it. quick checklist for the patch:
- change fallback group -> `contractor-limited`
- add an allowlist for `admins` that prevents assignment via fallback
- emit a high-severity audit event if any fallback attempts to assign a privileged group

maya: creating PR now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/scim-sync/pull/984 (WIP). I'll add the checklist items and the dry-run plan in the PR description.

jordan: awesome. once PR is up i'll kick off the staging dry-run and attach the export here. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — will ping when PR and staging run are ready. tagging @lee for product signoff when you have a minute.

lee: ack, will review later today.

samir: also, note for postmortem: consider adding a pre-sync validation that blocks any mapping that would produce `admins` for external identities. low-effort and high ROI.

maya: noted, will add to the PR and an issue for follow-up.

deploy-bot: reminder: next scheduled scim-sync maintenance window 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC.

security-bot: logging note: when you paste audit exports here, please redact full emails in public channels (use `contractor+eng@example.com` style or replace domain). thanks!

maya: good call — i replaced the real email above. continuing in PR thread. :lock:
